p: be your consolations: Your diligent marking of my words will be to me a great consolation.
were so: As though he would say, I do not talk with man but with God, who will not answer me, and therefore my mind must be troubled.
mouth: He charges them as though they were not able to comprehend his feeling of God's judgment, and exhorts them therefore to silence.

live: Job proves against his adversaries that God does not punish the wicked immediately, but often gives them long life and prosperity, so we must not judge God just or unjust by the things that appear to our eyes.
like a flock: They have healthy children and in those points he answers to that which Zophar alleged before.
go down to the grave: Not being tormented with long sickness.

knowledge of thy ways: They desire nothing more than to be exempt from all subjection that they should bear to God, thus Job shows his adversaries, that if they reason only by that which is seen by common experience the wicked who hate God are better dealt withal than they who love him.
hand: It is not their own, but God only lends it to them.
is far from me: God keep me from their prosperity.
His eyes shall see his destruction: When God recompenses his wickedness, he will know that his prosperity was vanity.
God knowledge: Who sends to the wicked prosperity and punishes the godly.
dieth in his full strength: Meaning, the wicked.
dieth in the bitterness of his: That is, the godly.
the dust: As concerning their bodies: and this he speaks according to the common judgment.
house of the prince: Thus they called Job's house in derision concluding that it was destroyed because he was wicked.
not asked them that go by: Who through long travailing have experience and tokens of it, that is, that the wicked prosper, and the godly live in affliction.
destruction: Though the wicked flourish here, yet God will punish him in the last day.
to his face: Though men flatter him, and no one dares to reprove him in this world, yet death is a token that he will bring him to an account.
clods of the valley shall be: He will be glad to lie in a slimy pit, who before could not be content with a royal palace.
ye me in vain: Saying that the just in this world have prosperity and the wicked adversity.
